name: Clownfish
description: Bright orange reef fish with white stripes.
funFact: Did you know? Clownfish can change their gender! All clownfish are born male, and the largest one in the group becomes female.
ecologyRole: Lives with sea anemones and helps keep them clean while the anemone protects the fish.
threats: Coral reef damage, aquarium trade, and warming oceans that bleach anemones.
conservationTip: Protect coral reefs and never take wild clownfish for home tanks.
diet: Algae, tiny plankton, and leftover food from their anemone

name: Angelfish
description: Graceful blue fish with tall fins.
funFact: Cool fact: Angelfish are very territorial! They defend their coral homes from other fish with bold colors and big fins.
ecologyRole: Grazes sponges and algae, helping keep reef surfaces balanced.
threats: Overfishing for aquariums and habitat loss when reefs die.
conservationTip: Support reef-safe sunscreen and coral restoration projects.

name: Jellyfish
description: Transparent, pulsing creature that glows in the deep.
funFact: Incredible! Jellyfish are about 95% water. They have no brain, heart, or bones — just a simple nervous system that helps them sense the world.
ecologyRole: Eats plankton and tiny animals; becomes food for sea turtles and ocean sunfish.
threats: Plastic bags look like jellyfish and can kill turtles that eat them by mistake.
conservationTip: Keep plastics out of the ocean so turtles never confuse trash with jellies.
diet: Plankton, tiny fish, and small crustaceans

name: Reef Shark
description: Sleek predator that keeps reef food webs healthy.
funFact: Amazing! Sharks have been swimming the oceans for over 400 million years — longer than dinosaurs!
ecologyRole: Apex predator that keeps fish populations healthy by hunting weak or sick animals.
threats: Shark finning, overfishing, and accidental catch in nets.
conservationTip: Sharks need our help — healthy oceans need healthy shark populations.

name: Seahorse
description: Tiny horse-headed fish that clings to seagrass.
funFact: Wow! Male seahorses give birth! The female leaves eggs in the male's pouch, and he carries them until they hatch.
ecologyRole: Eats tiny crustaceans among seagrass, helping control small critter populations.
threats: Seagrass loss, bycatch, and the traditional medicine trade.
conservationTip: Protect seagrass meadows — they are seahorse nurseries.

name: Sea Turtle
description: Ancient ocean traveler with a hard shell.
funFact: Ancient! Sea turtles have been around for about 110 million years. Some can hold their breath for hours while resting.
habitat: Open ocean, reefs, and nesting beaches
ecologyRole: Grazes seagrass which keeps meadows healthy; beaches depend on nesting turtles.
threats: Plastic bags, fishing nets, beach lights, and climate change affecting nests.
conservationTip: Turn off beach lights during nesting season and never leave fishing line behind.

name: Octopus
funFact: Mind-blowing! Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood. They can change color and texture in an instant to hide.
ecologyRole: Clever hunters that control crab and shellfish numbers on rocky reefs.
threats: Overfishing and pollution in coastal waters.
conservationTip: Give octopuses space in the wild — watch, don’t take.

name: Manta Ray
funFact: Amazing! Manta rays are the largest rays in the ocean and can leap several feet out of the water!
ecologyRole: Filter-feeds on plankton, linking tiny ocean life to big open-water ecosystems.
threats: Fishing nets, boat strikes, and demand for gill plates.
conservationTip: Choose eco-friendly tourism — never chase or touch wild mantas.

name: Giant Squid
description: Deep-sea giant with eyes the size of dinner plates.
funFact: Giant squid eyes can be as big as a human head — the largest eyes in the animal kingdom!
ecologyRole: Deep-sea predator and prey for sperm whales.
conservationTip: Protect the deep ocean — so little of it has ever been explored.

name: Parrotfish
funFact: Parrotfish crunch coral and poop out sand — a single fish can make hundreds of pounds of beach sand a year!
ecologyRole: Grazes algae so corals can grow; helps build sandy beaches.
conservationTip: Healthy parrotfish mean healthier reefs — protect both.
diet: Algae growing on coral and rocks

name: Blue Tang
description: Electric-blue reef grazer with a yellow tail.
funFact: Blue tangs sleep in reef crevices at night and can raise a spine on their tail for protection!
ecologyRole: Eats algae that could smother coral if left unchecked.
conservationTip: Wild blue tangs belong on reefs — choose captive-bred pets only if you keep aquariums.

name: Lanternfish
description: Tiny glowing fish of the twilight zone.
funFact: Lanternfish make their own light (bioluminescence) and may be the most numerous vertebrates on Earth!
ecologyRole: Moves carbon and energy between the surface and the deep every night.
threats: Deep fishing and climate change shifting ocean layers.
conservationTip: What happens in the deep affects the whole planet — protect deep habitats too.

name: Cleaner Shrimp
description: Tiny reef doctor that cleans other fish.
funFact: Fish line up at 'cleaning stations' so cleaner shrimp can nibble parasites off their scales!
ecologyRole: Removes parasites and dead skin — a living health service for the reef.
threats: Reef destruction and collection for aquariums.
conservationTip: Even the smallest animals keep the reef healthy — size does not equal importance.
diet: Parasites and leftover food bits on fish

name: Butterflyfish
description: Bright, disc-shaped reef fish that pairs often swim together.
funFact: Many butterflyfish mate for life and sleep tucked into the coral at night!
ecologyRole: Nips coral polyps and tiny invertebrates — part of the reef's busy cleaning crew.
conservationTip: Healthy coral means healthy butterflyfish — protect the reef and they thrive.
